import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
data = pd.read_csv('slice_observations.csv')
selected = data[data['eligible'].eq(True) & data['long_distance'].eq(True)].dropna(subset=['error','loss'])
errors = selected['error'].astype(bool).to_numpy()
losses = selected['loss'].to_numpy()
ref_errors = selected['reference_error'].astype(bool).to_numpy()
ref_losses = selected['reference_loss'].to_numpy()
error_count = np.count_nonzero(errors)
error_probability = np.mean(errors)
loss_mean = np.mean(losses)
loss_std = np.std(losses, ddof=0)
reference_probability = np.mean(ref_errors)
reference_mean = np.mean(ref_losses)
reference_std = np.std(ref_losses, ddof=0)
result = {'eligible_count':len(losses),'error_count':error_count,'error_probability':error_probability,'loss_mean':loss_mean,'loss_std':loss_std,'reference_error_probability':reference_probability,'reference_loss_mean':reference_mean,'reference_loss_std':reference_std,'finding':'Long-distance failures recur in this predefined validation group; this descriptive comparison does not establish a cause.'}

segments.label: How overall improvement hides language-slice gaps
segments.summary: In this synthetic example, underlying fraud is equally common across languages. An English-centric description-quality score is lower for Hindi and Hinglish descriptions, and adding it improves overall fraud detection. The highest-scoring 10% of cases are flagged. Regional flag rates look nearly identical because languages are distributed evenly across regions. Language-specific detection tells a different story: the model detects 33.5% of fraud overall, but only about one-fifth of English-language fraud, over 40% of Hindi-language fraud, and more than half of Hinglish-language fraud. Overall improvement therefore coexists with uneven slice performance, including missed English-language fraud and burdens on innocent Hindi- and Hinglish-speaking customers.

blocks.group_title: Overall improvement and uneven slice performance

bridge.before: Watch how similar regional flag rates conceal different language-specific fraud detection rates. These are distinct measurements in a synthetic example; overall improvement does not guarantee consistent performance across slices.
bridge.after: The clip demonstrates uneven slice performance, but does not provide eligible counts, explain population representativeness, or teach NumPy mean and standard deviation. The text supplies those reporting requirements, limitations, and calculations.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
data = pd.read_csv('slice_observations.csv')
a = data[data['eligible'].eq(True) & data['zone'].eq('A')].dropna(subset=['error','loss'])
b = data[data['eligible'].eq(True) & data['zone'].eq('B')].dropna(subset=['error','loss'])
a_errors = a['error'].astype(bool).to_numpy()
b_errors = b['error'].astype(bool).to_numpy()
a_losses = a['loss'].to_numpy()
b_losses = b['loss'].to_numpy()
a_probability = np.mean(a_errors)
b_probability = np.mean(b_errors)
a_mean = np.mean(a_losses)
b_mean = np.mean(b_losses)
a_std = np.std(a_losses, ddof=0)
b_std = np.std(b_losses, ddof=0)
result = {'A':{'eligible_count':len(a_losses),'error_probability':a_probability,'loss_mean':a_mean,'loss_std':a_std},'B':{'eligible_count':len(b_losses),'error_probability':b_probability,'loss_mean':b_mean,'loss_std':b_std},'limitation':'Observed validation slice gap only; population disparity is not established.'}

public.prompt: Report each record in declared order as system/scope:FPR=x.xxxx,FNR=x.xxxx,harm=x.xxxx,validation_fraction=x.xxxx,deployment_weight=x.xxxx. Add ,weighted_harm=x.xxxx for affected_subgroup rows only. Compute rates from counts and harm from supplied deployment class probabilities and costs; guard empty groups with undefined. Validation fraction is subgroup count / matched overall count (overall rows report 1.0000); deployment weighting is independent of that fraction. Separate records with "; ". The predeclared improvement rule is: affected-subgroup harm strictly decreases, overall harm does not increase and satisfies the fixed overall cost bound, and overall cost satisfies the fixed bound. Operating requirements are not supplied here; retaining a mitigation remains conditional on checking them separately. Append "; decision=" followed by "recommend supplied mitigation for measured validation harm reduction, conditional on unsupplied operating requirements" if the rule passes, else "do not retain supplied mitigation under the declared improvement rule"; then append "; representation beyond supplied sample is not established; operating eligibility and subgroup suitability remain unresolved without their separate criteria". This improvement verdict does not assert subgroup acceptance or universal suitability. Put the complete report in AZ2 as one formula; headers are in row 1 and all registry columns are shown in their original order.
